CH-35 gives an activation energy of 75.2 kJ/mol for the wet-cake hold-time model. Section 9 then states:

> a 10 K excursion above the nominal 298 K roughly doubles the degradation rate

This understates the temperature sensitivity implied by CH-35. Using the Arrhenius relation,

\[
\frac{k_2}{k_1}=\exp\left(\frac{E_a}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_1}-\frac{1}{T_2}\right)\right)
\]

with:

- \(E_a = 75.2\,\text{kJ/mol} = 75200\,\text{J/mol}\)
- \(R = 8.314462618\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\)
- \(T_1 = 298.15\,\text{K}\)
- \(T_2 = 308.15\,\text{K}\)

gives:

\[
\exp\left(\frac{75200}{8.314462618}\left(\frac{1}{298.15}-\frac{1}{308.15}\right)\right)
= 2.6763
\]

Concrete expected output: a 10 K rise from 298.15 K to 308.15 K increases the predicted degradation rate by about **2.7-fold**, not “roughly doubles”.
